text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: redis-cache-prod - connected_clients >= 90% (rule: redis.maxclients). PD incident: PD-48219. https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PD-48219 :rotating_light:

Amy: Acked. I'm the primary oncall, looking now.

PagerDuty: Alert details: metric redis.connected_clients (redis-cache-prod) breaching threshold. Current: 1910, threshold: 1728 (90%).

Amy: quick triage - latency on cached requests up, errors observed in frontend logs (504 / upstream timeout).

Dave: any recent deploys?

Amy: No deploys in the last hour. Traffic spike starting ~10m ago from embedding ingestion.

Lina: I'm seeing a flood of short-lived connections from the embedding-workers pool. Might be retry amplification.

Amy: running quick redis checks:
```
$ redis-cli -h redis-cache-prod INFO clients | egrep 'connected_clients|maxclients'
connected_clients:1910
maxclients:2048
```

Amy: CLIENT LIST shows a lot of ephemeral connections, many from the embeddings fleet (10.0.72.*).

Amy: Impact: small fraction of requests start to queue and sometimes fail with 5xx when Redis refuses connections. Customers using vector-embeddings ingest are affected.

PG SRE: Are Postgres connections also elevated? Could be cascade (workers opening DB + Redis).

Amy: psql check shows pgbouncer is also near limit but not critical. We should still keep DB team in the loop.

Dave: immediate mitigation ideas:
- throttle/gradually shed non-critical embedding ingestion traffic at edge
- enable app-side connection pooling/keepalive to cut connection churn
- short-term increase of redis client limit if safe
- divert heavy write-only traffic to a degraded path (read-only fallback)

Amy: I've started throttling ingestion via the API gateway rule (rolled to 10% sample -> 1% -> 0% for heavy clients) to reduce connection churn. Pushing config now.

Amy: Config snippet I applied:
```json
{"gateway":{"routes":[{"id":"/ingest/embeddings","rate_limit":{"enabled":true,"requests_per_minute":60}}]}}
```

Amy: Also enabled keepalive and connection pooling flag for embeddings service via feature flag so workers reuse connections. Rolling to 10% of pods now.

Lina: Good call. I'm going to kick a targeted restart for the few worst offenders (workers with crash-looping retry loop) after they drain.

Amy: Quick check: I can bump redis maxclients temporarily with `CONFIG SET maxclients 4096` but that requires kernel/ulimit and may mask the underlying churn. Thoughts?

Dave: If config set is allowed and we have headroom on file descriptors on the host, it's an acceptable short-term stopgap. But prefer to reduce churn first to avoid hitting other limits.

Amy: I ran `CONFIG GET maxclients` and `CONFIG SET maxclients 4096` succeeded on the primary. Clients metric dropped slightly as retries settled.

Amy: Command & output:
```
$ redis-cli -h redis-cache-prod CONFIG GET maxclients
1) "maxclients"
2) "2048"
$ redis-cli -h redis-cache-prod CONFIG SET maxclients 4096
OK
$ redis-cli -h redis-cache-prod INFO clients | egrep 'connected_clients|maxclients'
connected_clients:1950
maxclients:4096
```

Amy: After `CONFIG SET` we saw some headroom; errors reduced but still seeing elevated latency. Continuing telemetry.

PG SRE: I'll pre-warm an extra pgbouncer pool just in case Postgres sees follow-on load.

Lina: I'm also throttling the retry loop in the worker config to exponential backoff x3, rolling now.

Amy: Noting customer impact summary for comms: some ingestion requests were delayed or returned 5xx for ~6-12 minutes during peak. No data loss observed; retries were mostly successful after backoff.

Dave: Any alerts from Sentinel/replication?

Amy: Sentinel is fine. No failovers. Replicas are healthy. This is connection saturation, not memory/eviction.

PagerDuty: Alert acknowledged by Amy at 1755550005. Escalation suppressed after ack.

Lina: I'll keep watch for 30m, then hand off to night oncall if stable. I want a follow-up to harden: connection reuse in embedding client library, add early throttling on heavy API keys, and a postmortem to review backup capacity.

Amy: Created a quick ticket: https://jira.local/RED-9876 - "Redis connection churn during embeddings ingest - followup". Assigning to eng-infra + SDK team.

Dave: Suggested action items (captured):
- enforce app-side connection pooling (client libs)
- add per-key rate limits for high-throughput ingestion
- add a golden path runbook to safely bump maxclients and check host fd limits
- add an automated detection for high churn (many short-lived clients)

Amy: For handoff: Lina will be primary for next 4h. I'm marking PD incident resolved for immediate impact, keeping an eye on metrics.

Lina: Acknowledged. I'll post a short follow-up summary in #incidents with graphs and planned mitigations.

Amy: Closing notes: PD incident resolved at 1755551320 (suppressed after mitigations). Handed off to Lina for monitoring and post-incident work.

Lina: Quick status 30m later - metrics stable, connected_clients ~420, no new 5xx. Leaving a note to do the postmortem tomorrow. :white_check_mark:

Amy: Thanks everyone.

PG SRE: Thanks — will coordinate DB-side follow-ups if anything crops up.

PagerDuty: Incident PD-48219 closed by Amy.
